clue.text: Almost unhappy about a good story

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for unhappy is cut off

parts.note: unhappy means sad

indicators.note: about here means the pair of pieces after it are turned round

explanation.surface: Someone slightly gloomy about a fine tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts the last letter, D; 'about' turns round the pair A and G (good) to give GA.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long narrative, often a family chronicle or heroic tale.

clue.text: Went into business with seconds, cheaply renovated

parts.note: tarted up means done up in a cheap, showy way

explanation.surface: A shop opened selling seconds after a cheap refurbishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tarted up' is British informal for smartened up cheaply or gaudily.
explanation.definitionFit: Started up means launched a company or set up a venture.

clue.text: No memory of leading as a strain?

parts.note: ahead means leading, in front
as means like
a sieve is used to strain, so stands for a strainer

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about whether being in front counts as a strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strain' with the '?' is a strainer, a sieve. The phrase describes someone who forgets everything, as if memories drain away.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a very poor memory is said to forget things the moment they hear them.

clue.text: The person who might seek out bargain fish?

definitions.text: The person who might seek out bargain fish?

parts.words: The person who might seek out bargain fish?
parts.note: read literally, a fish bought at a bargain price; in the other sense, a stingy person who always hunts for a deal

explanation.walkthrough: The skate is a flat fish; a cheap one would be a bargain, and the whole phrase is also the word for a miser.
explanation.definitionFit: A miserly person is notorious for chasing bargains and refusing to spend.

clue.text: Drink one after song captivates one!

indicators.note: after means the first one is placed following the rest
captivates means the song word holds the second one inside it

parts.note: a chant is a simple song
I is the Roman numeral for one
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone toasting a performance with a glass after a captivating song.
explanation.walkthrough: CHANT takes in I to give CHIANT, then the first 'one' (I) goes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany.

clue.text: Oriental trees are rubbish!

parts.note: oriental means eastern, abbreviated E
yew and ash are two kinds of tree
yew and ash are two kinds of tree

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses Eastern trees as worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trees' supplies two trees, YEW and ASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is informal for nonsense or humbug meant to deceive.

clue.text: Set down quietly to get trimmed

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical instruction to play quietly
lopped means cut back or trimmed

explanation.surface: A hedge cut back with little noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Plopped means dropped or put down casually with a soft sound.

clue.text: Remain calm when innkeepers shoot at random

indicators.note: at random means the letters of innkeepers shoot are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: Stay cool when pub landlords start firing shots wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at random' rearranges INNKEEPERS SHOOT. The answer is a British idiom urging someone not to lose their temper.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means don't get angry or excited, stay composed.

clue.text: Celebrate former auction item turning up

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the word for an auction item is read bottom to top

parts.note: a lot is an item put up for sale at auction

explanation.surface: Praising an old piece that has resurfaced at auction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' turns LOT to TOL in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly or glorify.

clue.text: He's stuck in a nightclub — but how?

definitions.text: He's stuck in a nightclub — but how?

indicators.note: stuck in tells us the letters of He's are lodged inside the next pieces

parts.note: a dive is a seedy nightclub or bar
taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A puzzled man finds himself glued inside a club and wonders how.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nightclub' points to dancing, but a dive is any seedy bar. 'stuck in' lodges HES in A DIVE, and 'but how?' makes the whole clue ask what keeps him there.
explanation.definitionFit: Glue or any sticky substance is what keeps something stuck fast.

clue.text: Old idiot — taking in oriental cat!

indicators.note: taking in means the word for idiot swallows the next piece

parts.note: a clot is a British colloquial word for a fool
oriental means eastern, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: An old fool keeps an exotic Eastern cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocelot is a spotted wild feline of the Americas.

clue.text: Hamstring perhaps means heavyweight must accept the finish

indicators.note: must accept means the heavyweight word holds the finish word inside it

parts.note: a ton is a heavy weight
the finish is the end

explanation.surface: A boxer's injury suggests the heavyweight has to accept the fight is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamstring' is a noun here: one of the tendons behind the knee, hence 'perhaps' for an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The hamstrings are a set of cords joining thigh muscle to bone at the back of the knee, an example of the anatomical type.

clue.text: Permission for a couple of coppers to run cricket ground

parts.note: coppers are pennies, p each, so two of them give PP
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run
The Oval is a famous London cricket ground

explanation.surface: Two police officers seek leave to jog round a cricket pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police but means copper coins, pennies (p). THE OVAL is a London cricket ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Approval is consent or sanction, so getting it means being allowed to act.

clue.text: Girl from Austria with two names

parts.note: A is the international vehicle code for Austria
N is an abbreviation for name, so two give NN

explanation.surface: An Austrian girl with a double-barrelled name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ann is a female first name.

clue.text: Belittle beautiful girl in car? Quite the opposite!

indicators.note: in would put the girl inside the car, the container signal
quite the opposite reverses the stated roles, so the car goes inside the girl instead

parts.note: dish is slang for an attractive person
the Mini is a small British car

explanation.surface: A pretty girl sits in a little car, or is it the other way round?
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' alone would put the car inside the girl's word; 'Quite the opposite!' flips which piece goes inside which. Dish is old slang for an attractive person; the Mini is a small British car.
explanation.definitionFit: To diminish something is to make it seem smaller or less important, to run it down.

clue.text: Giving new colour with edgy design around home

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the home piece
design suggests the letters of edgy are arranged into a new pattern

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A trendy pattern is used to recolour things around the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'design' rearranges EDGY to DYEG, and 'around' puts IN (at home) between its E and G.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyeing is the process of changing a fabric's colour by soaking it in pigment.

clue.text: Eco-friendly support for the dollar

parts.note: green means environmentally friendly
to back is to support

explanation.surface: Environmental campaigners shore up the US currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenback is an American nickname for the dollar bill, from its green reverse side.

clue.text: Spiritual leader quietly performing rites

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical instruction to play quietly

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters of rites are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A holy man softly conducts ceremonies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing' looks like part of the rites picture, but it is the signal to rearrange RITES, giving RIEST after P.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest is an ordained minister who guides a congregation in faith.

clue.text: Regret genuine leader being dropped

indicators.note: leader being dropped means the opening letter of the word for genuine is removed

parts.note: genuine means true

explanation.surface: Sorrow when a real chief is sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: TRUE loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue is to feel sorry about or wish undone.

clue.text: Language from label on a record

parts.note: a tag is a label
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: A word on a label stuck to a gramophone record.
explanation.definitionFit: Tagalog is the main tongue spoken in the Philippines.

clue.text: Where to find rickety tables full of spectacles?

definitions.text: Where to find rickety tables full of spectacles?

indicators.note: full of means the rearranged letters are filled with the spectacles piece
rickety suggests the letters of tables are shaky and fall into a new order

parts.note: OO looks like a pair of glasses

explanation.surface: A place to pick up wobbly old furniture and second-hand glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rickety' rearranges TABLES to BTSALE, with OO inside after the B. A car boot sale is a British market where people sell junk from their car boots.
explanation.definitionFit: A car boot sale is a flea market where cheap used goods are sold from parked cars.

clue.text: Worst individual is one who speaks at the match

definitions.text: one who speaks at the match

parts.note: to worst someone is to beat them, the same as to best
a man is an individual person

explanation.surface: The poorest performer is the one making a speech at the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worst' as a verb means defeat, the same as 'best'. 'match' is a wedding, not a game.
explanation.definitionFit: At a wedding the groom's chief attendant traditionally gives a speech.

clue.text: Trips cancelled in case of gastroenteritis

parts.note: out means cancelled or off

indicators.note: case of means the outer letters of gastroenteritis, its casing

explanation.surface: Holidays called off because of a stomach bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' takes G and S, the first and last letters of 'gastroenteritis'.
explanation.definitionFit: Outings are short excursions or day trips.

clue.text: Creates chaos about a source of garbled communications

indicators.note: about means the chaos word goes round the next pieces

parts.note: to create chaos is to make a mess, so messes

indicators.note: source of means just the opening letter of garbled is used

explanation.surface: Someone muddles a source and the resulting messages come out scrambled.
explanation.walkthrough: MESSES goes round A plus G, the first letter of 'garbled'.
explanation.definitionFit: Messages are items of communication sent from one person to another.

clue.text: Madonna's first song from an opera?

definitions.text: Madonna's first song from an opera?

indicators.note: first means just the opening letter of Madonna's

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in an opera

explanation.surface: The pop star's debut single taken from an operatic work.
explanation.walkthrough: M plus ARIA. The '?' covers that 'Maria' is from West Side Story, a musical rather than an opera; Maria is also another name for the Madonna.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria is the famous love song from the musical West Side Story.

clue.text: Patina that's unusual in a snake

indicators.note: unusual means the letters of patina are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: A snake with a strange sheen on its scales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges PATINA.
explanation.definitionFit: The taipan is a highly venomous Australian serpent.

clue.text: Show delight, accepting first of awards

indicators.note: accepting means the delight word takes in the next piece

parts.note: to revel is to take delight

indicators.note: first of means just the opening letter of awards

explanation.surface: Displaying joy on being given the top prize.
explanation.walkthrough: REVEL takes in A, the first letter of 'awards'.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal is to disclose or make visible.

clue.text: A fool accepted by the mafia with a place in Canada

indicators.note: accepted by means the first pieces are taken inside the mafia word

parts.note: the Mob is a common name for the Mafia
nit (nitwit) is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: A simpleton taken in by gangsters ends up somewhere in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepted by' puts the first two pieces inside the mafia word; the second 'a' then follows outside, so 'a place' is not all definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Manitoba is one of the Canadian prairie provinces.

clue.text: Vegetables that might ensure a big stew

indicators.note: stew suggests the letters of ensure a big are stirred together into a new order

explanation.surface: Things you might use to make a large stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew' rearranges ENSURE A BIG.
explanation.definitionFit: Aubergines, called eggplants in America, are purple-skinned vegetables.

clue.text: One might inform rescue vessel to get bearing first

indicators.note: first means the bearing piece is placed before the vessel

parts.note: N, north, is a compass bearing
Noah's ark rescued the animals from the flood

explanation.surface: An informer tells the lifeboat to take a compass bearing first.
explanation.definitionFit: A nark is British slang for a police informer.
